Quarry and borrow areas would be located within the upper reservoir drainage area (Figure 1-4). A supplemental borrow area outside the reservoir has been designated for use in case the site within the reservoir proves to be inadequate. Any borrow areas not inundated by the reservoir would be sloped, terraced, and reforested upon completion of the project. The reservoir site would be cleared to an elevation of 2,315 feet, 5 feet above the reservoir full pool elevation. All other project lands including the transmission line right-of-way would be selectively cleared insofar as possible, with reseeding as soon as practical, and eventual reforesting wherever possible.
A 40-acre site outside the proposed project boundary would be used as a combination spoil area and construction yard. A future 525-kV switchyard is also planned for this area. Upon completion of the project, this 40-acre site would be reforested except for the switchyard site that would be stabilized and planted with grass or other ground rover until needed.
During land clearing operations and dam construction, sediment traps would be placed in the old stream beds to contain silt. A major settlement basin could be placed in Bad Creek, downstream of the dam site, to further minimize siltation and excessive turbidity in Howard Creek, if determined necessary.
Wells would be drilled as needed for drinking water supply. Water for other purposes would be drawn from Lake Jocassee.
A permanent paved access road approximately 4 miles long would extend from South Carolina State Highway 171 around the north side of the upper reservoir to the tunnel adits at the backwaters of Lake Jocassee. Temporary roads would be constructed for use during dam construction and related work. Upon completion of construction, all temporary roads would be reseeded or reforested as appropriate.
